segments.text: Let us start at the beginning. Where were you born?
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01

segments.text: Um, I was born in Busan, in a little house near the harbour, I think it was nineteen forty-six, in the spring.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: My mother always said the fishing boats were coming in the morning I was born, so there was a lot of noise, you know, and the midwife could hardly hear herself think.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Tell me about your father.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01

segments.text: My father repaired boats.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: He had big hands, really big, and he did not talk much at all.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: He would come home smelling of tar and sawdust, and he would sit by the door and take his boots off, and that was it, that was the whole conversation for the evening.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: But on Sundays he took me to the pier and we watched the ships.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: I loved those Sundays.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And your mother?
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01

segments.text: My mother sold fish at the market.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: She left before dawn and came home after sunset every single day, and her hands smelled of salt.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: She was the one who held the family together.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: She could count money faster than anyone I ever met, and she never learned to read, but nobody ever cheated her, not once.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Mm-hm.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01

segments.text: Yes, she was something.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: What was your house like?
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01

segments.text: We lived in a shack made of scrap boards, and the wind came through the walls in winter.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We had one stove for the whole family, so we all slept close to it.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: There were six of us in two rooms.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: I remember my brother Jaesung kept a little bird in a box under his bed, and he fed it rice, and it lived for almost two years.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Did you go to school?
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01

segments.text: I only finished fifth grade.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Um, we could not afford more.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: But my teacher, Mrs.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Han, said I had the most beautiful handwriting in the whole school, and she gave me a pencil box as a prize when I left.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: I still have that pencil box, it is in the cabinet in my bedroom.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: It has a picture of a crane on the lid.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: What happened after you left school?
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01

segments.text: At eighteen I started at a textile factory, and I gave my whole pay to my mother.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Every month, the whole envelope.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: She would put a little aside for me in a tin, and when I got married she gave me the tin, and there was enough in it for a sewing machine.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: That machine is what I started my own business with, many years later.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: When did you meet your husband?
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01

segments.text: I met Minho in nineteen sixty-six, at a church supper.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: He was so nervous that he spilled gravy all over his shirt, and I laughed, and he went red, and that was that.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We married in June of nineteen sixty-seven, in a small ceremony, because we did not have money for anything bigger.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Where did you live after you married?
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01

segments.text: We moved to Daegu, because Minho had found work at a printing house there.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The pay was better than the harbour.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We rented two rooms above a tailor's shop, and the tailor, Mr.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Baek, became like an uncle to us.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: He taught me to cut cloth, and that is how I started sewing for other people.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
